analysis_notes.gap_analysis: The source text of LM2 Torah 58 introduces five key concepts: צַדִּיק (the tzaddik/righteous person), אַיִן (nothingness — the state of self-nullification), יֵשׁ (existence/somethingness — having a fixed selfhood and location), הַשְׁגָּחָה פְּרָטִית (divine particular providence), and מָקוֹם (place/location). None of these appear in bechina-typed edges for this Torah (there are none in the dataset). The Rebbe's teaching structure is as follows: (1) A 'yesh' — something with fixed existence — cannot be in two places at once; when occupied here, it is absent elsewhere. (2) An 'ayin' — nothingness — has no place, and therefore is absent from nowhere. (3) The tzaddik who is subsumed in 'ayin' can therefore watch over the entire world simultaneously, just as God — infinitely transcendent — exercises particular providence over all creation. The relationships expressed are causal and analogical, not bechina equivalences: 'ayin' ENABLES omnipresence (eitza); God's transcendence IS THE MODEL for the tzaddik's oversight (analogy/proof); 'yesh' and 'ayin' are opposites, not shared-nature parallels. The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear in the text. No equating language appears anywhere. The reference to LM1 Torah 162 (about 'one who wants wisdom should turn south') is a cross-reference to a related teaching, not a bechina statement within this Torah. Therefore no additions to packages can be proposed — there are no packages to add to, and no bechina formulations in the source text that would warrant new package entries.
